title: Append-only stream chunker for lossless tenant merge and Loki/ELK compatibility
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Goal: Implement an append-only stream chunker that produces deterministic, lossless segments for multi-tenant log ingestion. The chunker must preserve per-tenant ordering, support idempotent replays (re-ingest after failure), and expose compact segment metadata for downstream sinks (Loki/ELK). Background: Current ingest path relies on variable-sized batches that can reorder entries under retries and backpressure, causing incorrect session/trace reconstruction in downstream systems. This ticket implements a chunking layer upstream of the fanout that ensures each chunk is an immutable, time-bounded segment with a monotonic sequence id and tenant affinity header. Acceptance criteria:
1) Chunk producer writes segments to internal store (S3-like or Kafka topic) with metadata: tenant_id, seq_start, seq_end, segment_uuid, approximate_time_range, schema_version.
2) Downstream fanout can rehydrate segments and guarantee append-only semantics; downstream writes to Loki and ELK preserve segment boundaries for dedup and idempotency.
3) System supports partial replay: mark segment as sealed and allow replay by segment_uuid.
4) Performance targets: end-to-end ingest latency increase < 3ms p50; throughput target sustained 2x current per-node with no more than 8% CPU overhead.
5) Automated tests (unit + integration) covering ordering, duplicate suppression, and replay scenarios.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use sequence numbers at the tenant-chunker boundary (monotonic per-tenant) to avoid global coordination. This makes the chunk metadata small and routing deterministic.
- Store segments as compressed newline-delimited JSON (jsonl.gzip) to balance parsing simplicity for ELK and Loki compatibility.
- Rely on a write-ahead manifest in Kafka topic for quick lookups and replay; long-term retention in object store for compliance.
- Backpressure: when chunk buffer reaches high watermark, apply tenant-priority shedding and pushback via ingress gRPC flow-control (prefer controlled latency over dropping).
- Kernel: chunk sealing is time- or size-based (whichever triggers first) to ensure predictable replay windows.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Spike complete: validated tenant-local monotonic seq approach. Benchmarked single-node chunker at 1.8M events/s in synthetic harness (internal perf repo). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-perf/pull/57

2025-01-20 - Design review with infra & compliance: agreed on dual-store (kafka manifest + s3 archive) for replay and legal retention. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Append-only+Segment+Design

2025-01-25 - Prototype implemented in ingest-proxy service. PR opened for chunker core logic; request review from @maria-gomez and @tyler-ops. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/302

2025-01-30 - Code review feedback: 1) expose segment UUID in header for downstream tracing; 2) add metric for 'segment_open_ms' and 'segment_seal_ms'; 3) add integration test for concurrent tenant writes. Addressed those in PR 302 (updates pushed).

2025-02-03 - QA: ran canary ingest on staging with 3 tenants (high, med, low qps). Observed expected ordering with sequence reassembly in downstream consumer. Two issues found: occasional duplicate when consumer restarted mid-segment -> added per-segment dedup token in manifest. Tracking as follow-up work.
2025-02-05 - Coordination: Planning canary rollout to production ingest-only nodes week of 2025-02-12. Ops runbook drafted (see artifacts).
release_plan: Phase 1: Merge chunker behind feature flag and enable for 10% of tenant traffic (ingest-only nodes). Monitor ordering/error dashboards for 72h. Phase 2: Increase to 50% with cross-checking dedup metrics and consumer correctness. Phase 3: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy reorder guard. Rollback via feature flag and consumer-level drop-by-segment UUID.
testing_notes: Integration tests simulate network partitions and consumer restarts; verify idempotency on replay and ordering on merge. Load test harness runs 24h sustained at target QPS. Test artifacts and synthetic traces located in /perf/chunker-tests/2025-01-18.
notes: Follow-up tickets: add segment-aware retention policy, segment compaction for high-cardinality tenants, and segment-level encryption at rest (KMS integration).
